hints.title: 2D Subgrid Enumeration Obstacle
hints.text: Checking every possible rectangular subgrid incurs O(R^3 * C^3) brute-force complexity. How can collapsing consecutive vertical ones into histogram bars reduce the 2D problem to repeated 1D queries?

hints.title: Row-by-Row Histogram Invariant
hints.text: Row r provides a base for histograms where bar heights equal consecutive '1's ending at row r. The maximal rectangle ending at or above row r is bounded by the largest rectangle in that 1D histogram.

hints.title: Histogram Monotonic Reduction Procedure
hints.text: Maintain a heights array of length C initialized to 0. For each row: if matrix[r][c] is '1', increment heights[c], else reset heights[c] = 0. Then compute the maximum rectangle for heights using a monotonic increasing index buffer. Track the global maximum area.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

complexity.notes: Reduces 2D grid to R instances of largest rectangle in histogram.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Enumerating all O(R^2 * C^2) rectangles and verifying cells takes O(R^3 * C^3) time.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Maintaining 1D column heights across rows requires only O(C) auxiliary space.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Connecting this 2D problem cleanly to the 1D largest rectangle in histogram monotonic stack problem.
